title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 51
paragraphs: Cleomenes, having said this, went off to his house. But Aristagoras took the suppliant's branch and went to the house of Cleomenes; and having entered as a suppliant, he asked Cleomenes to send away the child and listen to him—for Cleomenes's daughter was standing beside him, whose name was Gorgo, and she happened to be his only child, being now eight or nine years old. Cleomenes, however, told him to say what he wanted and not to hold back on the child's account. Then Aristagoras proceeded to promise him money, beginning with ten talents, if he would accomplish what he was asking for; and when Cleomenes refused, Aristagoras went on increasing the sums offered, until at last he had promised fifty talents, and at that moment the child cried out: “Father, the stranger will corrupt you if you do not leave him and go.” Cleomenes, pleased by the child's advice, went off into another room, and Aristagoras left Sparta altogether, and had no further opportunity to explain about the road up from the sea to the king's residence.
